column1: # lane/parity: the observation's ray cast drawn by the oracle (RayCast.java) against C's (raycast.c), row for row on
# pool-gate's recordings (make -C csrc/runtime raycast-parity; rcparity.sh), 2026-11-02. The rows' fields never see
# these: the client world's light, its chunk set and its entity copies are not in a row; the cast reads them.

column6: the cast drew the client world's living copies but the C client holds the ender dragon apart, as a pick object (pickobj.c PK_DRAGON), so no End frame had the dragon the Java client's world has; raycast.c entities() now adds it after the living copies

the C client's copies of the End's dragon and endermen arrive a tick or two after the Java client's around a checkpoint join or the portal (cp-end-s1 rows 5 and 6, s1chain-S23 row 3124; rows 16780 to 16783 at the exit went with master's lane/exitdiv). cp-end-s1 (lane/parity2): the checkpoint's dragon was isAirBorne (its entity runtime fields), which runs its tracker entry's update block off the every-third-tick phase; endfight_snapshot_dragon dropped the field, so C's tracker skipped the tick-2 move (to x 363/32) and the copy ran a move behind for rows 3 to 6; it reads it now (and pickobj_bind resumes a snapshot entry's recorded state, 7400cca9). s1chain-S23 row 3124 is parity-teleport

the C client world's sky light differs from the Java client's after a respawn (respawn-loop-s1 row 25: (183,70,227) sky 13 on Java, 9 in C; (180,72,228) 14 against 13); 37 of 6,135 rows at 16x16, 159 at 64x64; gold-g15-s42 from row 5845, 80 of 13,027 at 16x16, 81 at 64x64: at (-3037, 70 to 72, -1700) sky 6 to 8 on Java, 12 to 14 in C. lane/parity2, two causes: an older snapshot lacks WorldClient's previousActiveChunkSet, which the Java client had walked once a row from row 2 of its join, so C's first walk started two rows ahead (respawn-loop-s1's lava relit the client's sky at row 25, Java's at 27; session.c cw_walks_before rebuilds the set); and a ground-up chunk packet (S26PacketMapChunkBulk, S21PacketChunkData) carries no section without a block, which fillChunk nulls, but C's client copy kept the server's empty sections, so its light writes stayed there where Java's recreated a fresh section (world.c chunk_drop_empty_secs, on both the S21 and the bulk path)

the C client world's block light differs from the Java client's (s1chain-S8 row 1891: above (31,75,-64) block light 11 on Java, 7 in C); 25 of 5,134 rows at 16x16, 57 at 64x64; end-arrival-s1 row 455 at 64x64: the dragon's box lit at light index 0 on Java, 1 in C. lane/parity2: BlockLeaves.breakBlock and BlockLog's mark the leaves around with setBlockMetadataWithNotify(.., 4), no markBlockForUpdate, so no packet; C wrote them with flag 2 (world_set_meta_quiet), each an S23 whose relight on the client carried the lava's block light into chunk 12 of respawn-loop-s1; with the empty sections (parity-skylight) s1chain-S8 and end-arrival-s1 equal at both sizes

the C client world still holds chunk (10, 20) the Java client no longer draws from after the deaths' respawn (chat-deaths-s1 row 658: C's rays meet blocks at z 320, Java's the fog). lane/parity2: the respawn at row 208 queued the spawn square in sr->send_queue (the S26 path's copy of EntityPlayerMP.loadedChunks), and the walk off it at row 217 had PlayerInstance.removePlayer take (10, 20) out of loadedChunks with an S21 the client ignored (no chunk yet), but sr->send_queue kept it and its bulk went out at 221; the bulk path now skips a chunk the player manager no longer holds for the player (chunkload.c cl_player_holds), and bulks and S21s reach the client in the order sent

the C client kept a mob the player killed a tick past the Java client (night-s1 row 7092: a sheep at (161.05, 69, 256.71); combat-mobs-s1 row 2322: a cow at (164.08, 68, 255.92), hit at 2302; gold-g15-s42 rows 2200, 2212, 4315): the killing blow's S19 status 3 goes out from onDeath in the network tick, but C sent it at the next tick's tracker pass, so the copy's deathTime ran a tick behind; combat_server_attack now sends it with the blow

a bat's client copy stands at y 50.09375 on the Java client (a packet's 1/32 position) and 50.1 in C's (combat-mobs-s1 row 2322). lane/parity2: combat-mobs-s1 was already equal at both sizes on lane/parity2's start (master 3aede81c), and at row 2322 every entity box, the bat's at y 50.09375 included, is bit for bit Java's at 64x64; clientworld.c also keeps a hanging bat's box where its move left it (EntityBat moves posY alone), 9b8662c2

a warm pool member (Pool.java, rewound: "restored 94 of 71328") replayed gold-g15-s42 with a client world whose light differed from a fresh JVM's on rows 2 to 1548 (64x64 digests 1,549 rows apart; at row 2 sky 15 against 0 at (-2657, 76, -1664)), every row field equal; a fresh JVM (POOL=0) and C agree there. The rows never see the client light, so the pool's equivalence never caught it; rcparity replays fresh. lane/parity2: not reached; Pool.java's Rewind restores every static field's graph, so what leaks is outside it (the server thread's state, thread-locals, GL)

column6: the End endermen's client copies stand apart by up to 0.03 blocks, and a copy's box edge by 1 ulp, between the two clients (gold-g30-s42 row 6488: (26.4243, 59, -66.9584) on Java, (26.3979, 59, -66.9354) in C; s1chain-S23 row 1159: z -2.5716 against -2.5396); gold-g30-s42 5 rows, s1chain-S23 1, seen at 64x64 only. lane/parity2: gold-g30-s42's copy 12 is bit for bit Java's through row 6487; at 6488 C's moves one third of a 4/32 interpolation step (+0.0417, -0.0416) and Java's that plus (+0.0264, -0.0230), the motion its onLivingUpdate's moveEntityWithHeading applied: the S12 (211, -627, -184) Java's tracker sent enderman 1012 at 6487 (the oracle's --cw-pkts 1012) and C's did not. Both servers' motion was equal; the entry's last sent motion was not: EntityTrackerEntry.tryStartWachingThis takes the entity's motion as it (the S0F carries it, at 6418), but combat.c's try_start_watching kept the last S12 the entry made before anyone watched (at 6415), so 6487's change from it stayed under 0.02 squared; it takes the motion now. gold-g30-s42 equal at 64x64, s1chain-S23's row 1159 too (its one row left is parity-teleport)

s1chain-S23 row 3124 at 16x16: enderman 267 (standing at (-31.5, 61, -14.41)) leaves the Java client's cast range a row before C's. Both servers teleport it in tick 3124 and send the same S18 (x -1231) that tick (the oracle's --cw-pkts 267: S12, S18, S1C, S19 at 3124), but the Java client's copy is at (-50.70, 59, -32.74) after its own tick 3124, before that S18: an arrow's client copy (at (-31.84, 62.52, -15.86) at row 3123 on both sides) hit the enderman's copy, and EntityEnderman.attackEntityFrom has no isRemote guard, so the indirect damage ran teleportRandomly on the client copy's own Random (up to 64 tries, 128 portal particles). C's client arrow copies make no hit and its living copies keep no Random of their own (the enderman's draws two portal particles a tick too), so C's copy waits for the S18. A port: the arrow copy's entity hit on the client and each living copy's Random stream
